podcast.body: This pop funk jam was the accessible lead single from "Nothing Like the Sun," released at the urging of Sting's record label. It originated as a jingle Sting wrote for a Japanese beer commercial. The song reached number seven on the pop chart and cracked the top 40 on the R&B chart. "Sting wrote for a Japanese beer commercial."

srcs.source: Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia

podcast.body: This song originated as a jingle penned by Sting for a Japanese Kirin Beer commercial, which, by airing only in Japan, made it "essentially invisible to Western listeners" at the time. Sting later re-recorded this "funky ditty" for his acclaimed album "Nothing Like The Sun," and it became a hit, peaking at number 7 on the Hot 100 in December 1987. "In 1987, sting sneaked a jingle onto the charts by penning it for a Japanese commercial for Kirin Beer."
